source.title: Minimum Number of Operations to Make All Array Elements Equal to 1

teaching.hint: How does having even one value equal to one change the remaining task?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: Existing ones spread at one operation per other position. Without one, first manufacture it by folding the shortest contiguous interval with GCD one.
solution_outline.approach: If there are c ones, return n-c. Otherwise enumerate interval starts and extend a running GCD to find the shortest GCD-one interval of length L. If none exists return -1; otherwise return L-1+n-1.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: Each running GCD is exactly that original interval GCD; the best length is the shortest qualifying interval found. Current values in any operation sequence depend on original contiguous intervals.
solution_outline.correctness: Each write creates at most one new one, so existing c ones require at least n-c writes, attained by spreading. With no initial one, the first one must depend on a contiguous original block whose GCD is one. Combining its L or more original contributors through adjacent edges needs at least L-1 operations, followed by at least n-1 writes to create the other ones. Folding a shortest interval and then spreading achieves both bounds. If the whole-array GCD is greater than one, its common factor is invariant and prevents any one.
solution_outline.complexity: O(n^2 log V) time for GCD updates with maximum value V and O(1) auxiliary space.
solution_outline.pitfall: Checking only adjacent coprime pairs misses arrays whose shortest GCD-one interval has length greater than two.

common_wrong_turns: Checking only adjacent coprime pairs misses arrays whose shortest GCD-one interval has length greater than two.
source_fidelity_notes: Retained one-endpoint replacement, adjacency, positivity, and impossible result; did not treat operations as deleting elements.
